interface.title: NEURO-RX :: Drug Response Intelligence (Drug Response Prediction Engine v3.0)
interface.field: Pharmacogenomics / precision oncology (GDSC cancer cell-line drug sensitivity, EGFR inhibitors in lung cancer lines)
interface.stage_of_work: Exploratory analysis and modelling: finding biomarkers and checking a predictive model on preloaded screening data
interface.what_it_is_for: For a chosen EGFR inhibitor, find the genes whose expression correlates with drug sensitivity (FDR-corrected), find the most sensitive cell lines, and test a Random Forest that predicts LN(IC50) from expression on held-out cell lines.

data.note: Seed data loads locally with no upload. It has 25 genes and 19 training plus 5 held-out cell lines per compound. The held-out lines are H23, H1703, A549, H596 and H441. In every compound, EGFR is the only significant gene. The other 24 genes have nearly identical r (about −0.059 for Erlotinib, −0.099 for Osimertinib), so they sit on top of each other in the volcano plot, and only 2–3 points show (screens/004.webp, biomarkers.csv). The volcano y-value is capped at 12 for plotting: EGFR's real −log10 p is 13.6. The sensitive-lines table column is labelled 'IC50', but its values are on the LN(IC50) scale (negative values for Osimertinib). Unreconciled: after switching to Afatinib, screens/033.webp shows the Cell Line ID box reading H23 with Actual/Predicted 2.700 / 2.372, but the replay records exactly those values for A549 under Afatinib. A549 had been selected under Erlotinib just before the switch, so the selectbox label may reset to the first option after a compound change while the shown values still belong to the previous pick. This is not confirmed, so per-line values read straight after a compound switch should not be trusted.

features.name: Volcano plot with FDR-coloured hits, legend filter and CSV export
features.general: Plot each feature's effect size against its significance, with threshold lines. Colour the points that pass multiple-testing correction, hover to identify a feature, hide the non-significant group, zoom into crowded regions, and export the full statistics table.
features.specific: Volcano Scan: Pearson r against −log10(raw p), with dashed lines at p=0.05 and r=±0.2. Points are magenta when BH-FDR < 0.05. Hover gives gene, r and −log10 p (drawn capped at 12). Clicking 'False' in the legend hides the non-significant genes. Box-zoom, then double-click to reset. Summary cards show genes scanned, significant count and train/test sizes. Export Biomarkers downloads biomarkers.csv (Gene, Correlation, P_Value, P_Value_FDR, -log10_P_Raw, Significant, plot_y). The export rerun can leave the 'False' trace hidden again.
steps: click the legend to hide non-significant genes
drag a box to zoom, double-click to reset
press Export Biomarkers to download the CSV
serves_tasks: Find the features whose correlation with the response passes the multiple-testing threshold
Export the full table of statistics for each feature

features.name: Response distribution histogram with ranked most-responsive table
features.general: Show how a response measure is spread across all samples, next to a sortable table of the samples that respond most.
features.specific: Dose-Response tab: LN(IC50) histogram of all matched cell lines (hover shows bin range and count) above a 'Top 10 Most Sensitive Cell Lines' grid whose 'IC50' column holds LN(IC50) values. Clicking the IC50 header sorts ascending, then descending.
steps: click the column header to re-sort
serves_tasks: See how the response values are spread across all samples

features.name: Train-vs-held-out model scorecard with predicted-vs-actual scatter
features.general: Report a model's cross-validated training score next to its held-out test score and error, with a scatter of predicted against observed values and a fitted trend line through them. There is no y=x reference line, so agreement has to be judged from the axis values, not from distance to a diagonal.
features.specific: ML Predictor: Performance Telemetry cards (Cross-Val R² train, Test R² unseen, Test RMSE) and a Predicted vs Actual LN(IC50) scatter for the test lines with a magenta OLS trend line fitted to predicted vs actual (slope about 0.6 for Erlotinib, not y=x). Hover gives the values, box-zoom and Reset axes adjust the view, and the camera button exports a PNG.
steps: read the CV and test metrics
serves_tasks: Compare the model's cross-validated training score with its score on held-out data
Inspect predicted against observed values for the test set

features.name: Held-out sample prediction inspector
features.general: Pick one sample from the held-out set and see the model's prediction next to the measured value, with the signed error.
features.specific: Prediction Simulator: the Cell Line ID dropdown lists only test-set lines (H23, H1703, A549, H596, H441). The cards show Actual LN(IC50), Predicted LN(IC50) and an error badge. The selected line is not highlighted in the scatter, so you match it by hovering values. After a compound switch the box label may not match the values shown (see data note).
steps: open the Cell Line ID dropdown
serves_tasks: Compare the prediction for one unseen sample with its measured value

features.name: Global treatment (compound) selector driving every view
features.general: One sidebar choice of the treatment under study recomputes every downstream analysis: statistics, distribution, model and summary.
features.specific: The Target Compound selectbox (Erlotinib, Gefitinib, Afatinib, Osimertinib) reruns the volcano statistics, histogram, top-10 table, Random Forest and the Integrity biomarker table for that compound. Switching compound can send the view back to the Volcano Scan tab. Gefitinib breaks the model step (see not_done).

features.name: Methods-provenance panel with final significant-hit table
features.general: State the analysis's leakage safeguards as a fixed checklist, above a table of the features that pass the multiple-testing threshold, so a reader can audit how the hits were obtained.
features.specific: Integrity tab: lists split before statistics, train-only median imputation, BH-FDR on the training set and 5-fold CV, above a Top Biomarkers (FDR < 0.05) table with Gene, r and FDR (EGFR only, for every working compound).
steps: read the significant-hits table (Gene, r, FDR)
serves_tasks: Confirm how leakage was avoided and see the final list of significant features
